setup.fails.more: Why a tunnel may fail to open
faq.what.a: A tunnel puts an app from your laptop online straight from your computer, like ngrok without a middleman. The connection runs between your laptop and your own computer, so there is no outside service to pay for or keep running. You run one command on the laptop, and the tunnel shows up in the list when it connects. Nothing is sent from the Hub: the laptop opens the tunnel.
faq.twoWays.q: Should I put a laptop app online or bring a laptop service in?
faq.twoWays.a: Put a laptop app online when it is a web page or a WebSocket: it gets a web address on this computer. Bring a laptop service in for any other TCP service, such as a database: programs on this computer reach it, and it gets no public address. Public addresses carry web traffic only. Other TCP travels inside the tunnel's connection, and only into this computer. For example: put the web app you are building on your laptop online at an address on this computer, or bring the database on your laptop in so an app on this computer can use it.
faq.ports.q: Which port on the computer should I use?
faq.ports.a: Leave it empty and a free one is picked. A web address does not need a fixed port. Set one when programs on the computer need a port they can count on. Ports below 80 can't be used. Ports below 1024 work only if this computer's tunnel program allows them; if it refuses, leave the port empty.
faq.riskyPorts.q: Which ports does the Hub warn about?
faq.riskyPorts.a: The Hub warns when the laptop port or the computer port often belongs to a database or an admin screen: 5432, 3306, 6379, 27017, 9200, 2375, 2376, 5984, 11211, 22, 3389 and 5900. When you put an app online it also warns about 8080, 9000, 15672 and 8500. A port that is not listed is not called safe; the page just says nothing about it. Anyone who can open the address can use the service behind it.
faq.password.q: When do I tick the password box?
faq.password.a: Tick it only if the computer's access settings ask for a user name and password. The tunnel then signs in with them. The command asks for the password on the laptop, or reads it from HOODY_KIT_PASSWORD, and it is never part of the command. The box starts ticked when the Hub's own reads of the computer were refused.
faq.fails.q: Why did my tunnel fail to open?
faq.fails.a: Port in use: another program on this computer holds it. Pick another port, or leave it empty. Port held by another session: another laptop uses it, or one that dropped may come back for it. Pick another port, or leave it empty. Port refused: ports below 80 never work, and below 1024 only when the tunnel program allows them. Too many ports in one session: stop some first.
faq.notLoading.q: Why doesn't a web address load?
faq.notLoading.a: Usually one of three things: the app on the laptop is not running, so start it there; this computer's access settings refused you, so check them under Access settings; or this page is out of date, so press Refresh to read the list again.
faq.reconnecting.a: An address in that group is waiting for its session: a laptop reconnecting, or a session closing. If a Disconnect did not get an answer, the session may have disconnected and the tunnel program may still be closing it. Use Check again to look.
